blocks.content: Quiz: What does the <!DOCTYPE html> declaration in an HTML document signify?
Tap an option below to answer:
It tells the browser the document is written in HTML.
<!DOCTYPE html> is a declaration to the web browser that the given document is an HTML document.
<!DOCTYPE html> is a declaration to the web browser that the given document is an HTML document.
It instructs the browser to display web content.
While <!DOCTYPE html> is essential for browser interpretation, it does not instruct the browser to display content.
While <!DOCTYPE html> is essential for browser interpretation, it does not instruct the browser to display content.
It defines a portion of the webpage.
<!DOCTYPE html> doesn't define any portion but rather declares the document version to the browser.
<!DOCTYPE html> doesn't define any portion but rather declares the document version to the browser.
It includes metadata for the webpage.
The metadata for a page is typically found in the <head> section, not in the doctype declaration.
The metadata for a page is typically found in the <head> section, not in the doctype declaration.
